questions.question: What should you do when crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: Do not stop.
Pass slower vehicles.
Change lanes.
Put the vehicle in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not stop.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, never stop, change gears, pass other vehicles, or change lanes while crossing railroad tracks.

questions.question: What should you check on a cargo lift?

options.text: That the lift is loosely attached.
That the lift is not leaking.
That the lift is fully extended.
That the lift is the proper color.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the lift is not leaking.
questions.explanation: Check the cargo lift for leaks, damage, or missing parts. The lift must be fully retracted and locked securely.

questions.question: What should a school bus driver do while students load and unload?

options.text: Read a book.
Watch the students and the loading process.
Talk to other bus drivers.
Listen to the radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the students and the loading process.
questions.explanation: Watch students as they board and exit to make sure they do not get caught in doors or handrails. Also check that they move safely away from the bus after exiting.

questions.question: How should students board a school bus?

options.text: In a single-file line.
Two at a time.
In as large a group as possible.
However they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Students should board slowly in a single-file line while holding the handrails.

questions.question: What should students do when the bus approaches a stop?

options.text: Stay seated.
Stand up and get their belongings.
Walk to the front of the bus.
Ask the driver questions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay seated.
questions.explanation: Students must stay seated until told to move. Walking around while the bus is moving is unsafe.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on an expressway during the skills test?

options.text: Change lanes frequently.
Use your mirrors to check traffic.
Drive on the left side of the lane.
Drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors to check traffic.
questions.explanation: Keep proper lane position, spacing, and speed on the expressway. Always check your mirrors and look in all directions for traffic.

questions.question: When should you adjust the outside mirrors on a school bus?

options.text: Before the trip starts.
During the trip.
After students board.
After the trip ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the trip starts.
questions.explanation: Check and adjust all mirrors before starting your trip. Proper mirror adjustment keeps students and other vehicles safe.

questions.question: What causes you to lose points during the basic control skills test?

options.text: Crossing over an exercise boundary.
Pulling up one time.
Exiting the vehicle once to check your position.
Setting the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing over an exercise boundary.
questions.explanation: The examiner counts each time your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each mistake counts as an error against your score.

questions.question: When checking power steering fluid, which is NOT required?

options.text: Point out where the dipstick is located.
Check that there is enough fluid.
Make sure the fluid is above the full mark.
Make sure the fluid is above the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the fluid is above the full mark.
questions.explanation: Show where the dipstick is and confirm there is enough fluid. The level must be above the refill mark, not the full mark.

questions.question: What should you do when crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: Stop on the tracks.
Change gears.
Try to pass.
Stay in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Never stop, change gears, pass other vehicles, or change lanes while crossing railroad tracks.

questions.question: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, what should you do?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Pull forward to the right, then back in a straight line.
Pull forward to the left, then back in a straight line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, pull straight forward first. Then back up to the right. Your vehicle must fit completely within the parking space.

questions.question: What maneuver may be part of a basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.
Drive in a figure eight.
Alley dock.
Sound your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alley dock.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, are drivers allowed to exit the vehicle?

options.text: No, they are not permitted to stop and exit.
They are discouraged from exiting.
Yes, only if the vehicle is in reverse.
Yes, only if the vehicle is in neutral and the parking brake is set.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, only if the vehicle is in neutral and the parking brake is set.
questions.explanation: Before you exit the vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, put the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake. You may check the vehicle's position up to two times, except for straight line backing, where you may look only once.

questions.question: During the skills test, if you must stop before turning, what should you do?

options.text: Skid to a stop.
Stop after the stop line for a better view.
Let your vehicle roll slowly.
Keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead.
questions.explanation: When you must stop before turning, come to a smooth stop behind the stop line, crosswalk, or stop sign. Keep your front wheels aimed straight ahead and do not let your vehicle roll. Stop where you can still see the rear tires of the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: Are school buses equipped with ABS?

options.text: No, they are never equipped with ABS.
Only if they are in cold climates.
Yes, they may be equipped with ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they may be equipped with ABS.
questions.explanation: Most commercial vehicles made after 1998 or 1999 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). Many older buses also have ABS.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, what counts as a look?

options.text: Walking to the back of the vehicle to check its position.
Using side mirrors to check the vehicle's position.
Looking out of the driver's side window to check the vehicle's position.
Glancing over your shoulder to check blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walking to the back of the vehicle to check its position.
questions.explanation: A look happens when you open your door, leave your seat, and walk to the back of the vehicle to check its position. For straight line backing, you may look only once. For any other exercise, you may look up to two times.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, which of the following do you NOT need to show?

options.text: That the oil pressure gauge is working.
That the oil pressure warning light turns off or the gauge shows normal pressure.
That the oil temperature gauge rises to normal operating range, if equipped.
That the oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used.
questions.explanation: When checking the oil pressure gauge during a vehicle inspection, make sure it is working. The gauge should show normal or increasing oil pressure, or the oil pressure warning light should turn off. If the vehicle has an oil temperature gauge, it should gradually rise to normal operating range.

questions.question: What will the examiner score you on during the driving test?

options.text: How well-spoken you are.
How quickly you reach your destination.
Your general driving behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your general driving behavior.
questions.explanation: The examiner will score you on specific driving maneuvers and your general driving behavior. You must drive safely and responsibly. You must obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws. You must not cause any accidents or moving violations.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, which is NOT required?

options.text: Wear your safety belt.
Obey all traffic signs.
Complete the test without an accident.
Show that you can use your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that you can use your cell phone while driving.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, you must drive safely and responsibly. Wear your safety belt. Obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws. Complete the test without any accidents or moving violations.

questions.question: When checking engine belts during the vehicle inspection test, what must you do?

options.text: Check the belts for snugness, allowing up to three inches of play.
You do not need to identify the water pump belt.
Remove the air compressor belt.
Identify which items are not belt-driven, if any.

questions.correctAnswerText: Identify which items are not belt-driven, if any.
questions.explanation: When checking the engine during the vehicle inspection test, examine the power steering, water pump, alternator, and air compressor belts for cracks and fraying. Check the belts for tightness, allowing up to three-quarters of an inch of play at the center of each belt. If any of these items are not belt-driven, identify them and make sure they are working properly, not damaged or leaking, and are mounted securely.
